text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former prime minister, Tansu Ciller, has reversed her previous support for the military-backed eight-year education plan, saying religious schools should remain open.
- Turkish prosecutors have dropped an investigation into charges that Ciller spied for the CIA due to lack of evidence.
- The deputy chairman of the World Bank said his organisation could give Turkey up to $1.5 billion in credit over three years.
- Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz is determined to carry through the eight-year education plan, despite some opposition from within his own party.
- At a meeting of the National Security Council, Yilmaz's new government vowed to carry out a series of demands to counter Islamic activisim put forward by the military-dominated council in February.
- Leading brokerage companies working on the privatisation of Turk Telekom say the planned flotation cannot take place this year as the government wants.
- A group of four theology professors have prepared a report recommending further education for personnel employed by the directorate of religious affairs.
